question.problem:
A seller delivers bricks on pallets. One pallet contains $500$ bricks. The weight of a brick is normally distributed with a mean of $3\,\text{lb}$ and a standard deviation of $0.25\,\text{lb},$ while the weight of a pallet is normally distributed with a mean of $40\,\text{lb}$ and a standard deviation of $4\,\text{lb}.$ If one pallet with bricks is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs less than $1\,545\,\text{lb}?$ You may assume that the weights are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ | $\,0.7704\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ | $\,0.7995\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the weight of the $i$th brick, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a pallet. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(3,{0.25}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 500,
$$

and

$$
Y∼N(40,{4}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the weight of a randomly selected pallet with bricks. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{500}+Y,
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =500\cdot 3+40 \\  & =1\,540, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =500\cdot {0.25}^{2}+{4}^{2} \\  & =47.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(1\,540,47.25).
$$

In order to find $P(W<1\,545),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W<1\,545) & =P(Z<\frac{1\,545-1\,540}{\sqrt{47.25}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<0.73) \\  & =Φ(0.73)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.73)≈0.7673.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W<1\,545) & ≈Φ(0.73) \\  & ≈0.7673.\end{aligned}
$$
